f.title: Have a system documenting the GVP module objectives
f.statement: All pharmaceutical companies / MAHs whose products are registered and marketed in Oman must have a system in place for documenting the objectives laid down in the GVP modules: PV systems and their quality systems, PSMF, PV inspections, PV audits, risk management systems, management and reporting of adverse reactions, PSURs/PBRERs, post-authorisation safety studies, signal management, safety communication and risk minimisation measures. Pharmacovigilance obligations apply to all products available in Oman, registered and non-registered.

f.applicability: Products registered and marketed in Oman; the introduction states PV obligations apply to all products available in Oman, including registered and non-registered products

f.title: Maintain an appropriate PV system and report risk-benefit information fully and on time
f.statement: The MAH should ensure that it has an appropriate pharmacovigilance system in place to assume responsibility and liability for its products on the market and to ensure that appropriate action may be taken when necessary. The MAH should therefore ensure that all information relevant to the risk-benefit balance of a medicinal product is reported to the Department of Pharmacovigilance & Drug Information (DPV & DI) fully and on time in accordance with the guideline.
f.clause: 2. Responsibilities of MAH / Pharmaceutical Companies and QPPV

f.title: Provide educational materials in accessible formats and user-test them where feasible
f.statement: Ideally, educational materials should be available in a range of formats so that access is not limited by disability or internet access; when feasible, the appropriateness of the tool and media for the target audience should be user tested in advance.

f.title: Align educational material with approved product information; no promotional elements
f.statement: The content of any educational material should be fully aligned with the currently approved product information (SmPC and package leaflet) and should add to rather than duplicate it. Promotional elements, direct or veiled (logos, brand colours, suggestive images), should not be included; the focus should be on the risks and their management.
